title: How One Robot Learns to Move in Three Different Bodies
brief: A visual explanation of how a control model can transfer movement intelligence across different robot bodies instead of programming every joint from scratch. topic_candidates.title: The Password Can Leak One Microsecond at a Time
topic_candidates.query: NIST timing side-channel attack password validation
topic_candidates.brief: A premium cybersecurity explainer showing how software that stops checking a password at the first wrong character creates a measurable timing fingerprint. Viewers see an attacker statistically reconstruct a secret one character at a time, turning invisible delays into a practical breach.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Current demand: Very high, directly supported by the supplied seed “How Tiny Delays Reveal Your Password” at 960,659 views/day across US, GB, IN and ZA. Visual potential: Excellent—animated request timers, signal averaging and a password gradually resolving. Evidence strength: Strong; NIST defines timing as a side channel, and its NVD documents a real password-validation vulnerability exploitable through timing differences. Broad curiosity: High because the mechanism is counterintuitive and applies to websites, APIs and authentication systems. Novelty: Strong if framed around the statistical reconstruction process rather than simply warning about hacking. ([nvd.nist.gov](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2014-0984?utm_source=openai))

topic_candidates.title: The Hidden Skeleton Inside a Foldable Screen
topic_candidates.query: Samsung Display foldable OLED titanium plate durability micro holes crease
topic_candidates.brief: Explain why a foldable OLED is not merely a flexible sheet: beneath the pixels is a layered mechanical system that spreads stress, supports the bend and limits crease damage. The episode can visualize how microscopic holes, adhesive layers and a titanium support structure change where force travels.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Current demand: High, supported by repeated foldable-phone and durability signals, including the supplied seed “Is the iPhone fold’s durability cooked..” at 1,010,592 views/day and multiple foldable-phone trend entries. Visual potential: Excellent—cutaway animations, repeated-bend stress maps and microscopic crease simulations. Evidence strength: Strong for the engineering mechanism, with Samsung Display describing its reinforced titanium plate, hole-processing and adhesive structure. Broad curiosity: High because viewers understand the visible crease but rarely see the hidden load-bearing architecture. Novelty: Good; avoid a generic durability test and focus on the invisible mechanical stack that keeps a screen alive. ([global.samsungdisplay.com](https://global.samsungdisplay.com/31479?type=main&utm_source=openai))

topic_candidates.title: Why Morse Code Still Wins When the Radio Is Almost Dead
topic_candidates.query: ARRL Morse code narrow bandwidth weak signal noise advantage
topic_candidates.brief: Reveal the engineering reason a century-old signaling system can remain intelligible inside static: short, narrowband on-off pulses let receivers filter away much of the surrounding noise. Build the story around a simulated radio signal disappearing into noise, then recover it by narrowing the receiver and slowing the code.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Current demand: Medium-high, supported by the supplied Morse-code seed at 853,439 views/day across US, GB and ZA. Visual potential: Very strong—waterfall displays, bandwidth comparisons, noise injection and signal recovery create immediate before/after moments. Evidence strength: Strong; ARRL explains that CW/Morse occupies far less bandwidth than voice and that narrow filtering improves readability under weak-signal conditions. Broad curiosity: High because it turns a familiar historical code into a modern lesson in signal processing. Novelty: Strong if the focus is not Morse history or speed records, but the physics of why it survives interference. ([arrl.org](https://www.arrl.org/weak-signal-modes?utm_source=openai))
